title: Which Way Should an HVAC Air Filter Face?

seo.title: Which Way Should an HVAC Air Filter Face?
seo.meta_description: The arrow on an HVAC filter should point in the direction of airflow, toward the blower and into the equipment.
seo.search_intent: Determine which way an hvac air filter face and apply the equipment’s airflow markings correctly without forcing an incompatible installation.

excerpt: The arrow on an HVAC filter should point in the direction of airflow, toward the blower and into the equipment. The physical direction varies depending on whether the filter sits at a return grille or beside the air handler or furnace.
content_html:
The arrow on an HVAC filter should point in the direction of airflow, toward the blower and into the equipment. The physical direction varies depending on whether the filter sits at a return grille or beside the air handler or furnace.

Find the arrow printed on the filter frame

The arrow marks airflow, not simply which side should face outward. If the old filter was installed correctly, take a photo before removing it so you have a reference for the replacement.

At a return, air travels toward the equipment

At a wall or ceiling return grille, the arrow usually points into the duct. At a filter slot beside the unit, it points from the return duct toward the blower.

The support grid usually sits downstream

Many pleated filters have a reinforced side that resists suction. That support generally faces the blower, but the manufacturer’s airflow arrow is the authority if the design differs.

A backward filter can deform or perform poorly

If the filter bows, whistles, or fits poorly, turn the system off and check size, direction, and seating. Do not force an incorrectly sized filter into the rack.

faq.question: What does the arrow printed on an air-filter frame indicate?
faq.answer: The arrow marks airflow, not simply which side should face outward. If the old filter was installed correctly, take a photo before removing it so you have a reference for the replacement.

faq.question: Which way should the arrow point at a return grille or beside the equipment?
faq.answer: At a wall or ceiling return grille, the arrow usually points into the duct. At a filter slot beside the unit, it points from the return duct toward the blower.

faq.question: What should I do if the filter bows, whistles, or fits poorly?
faq.answer: If the filter bows, whistles, or fits poorly, turn the system off and check size, direction, and seating. Do not force an incorrectly sized filter into the rack.
